quest.title: Elixirs and Potions
quest.description: Timaeus, the alchemist from Mondstadt, is currently troubled by a certain research topic...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Agh, so close... C'mon, Timaeus, you can do this! You're going to create your first Smoldersleet Elixir within the next nine hours!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Timaeus? What are you doing, and why're you looking all serious?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: It's you two! It's been a while, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm currently trying to make Smoldersleet Elixir. I'll be occupying this Crafting Bench in the meantime, I'm afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Smoldersleet Elixir? Paimon's never heard that one before...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: This is a sort of mysterious medicine that has emerged of late. I only just discovered it, unexpectedly, in a certain academic tome.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: According to the author, the Smoldersleet Elixir originates in Liyue, and it can cause the strength of its user to multiply. Its efficacy is unmatched as well... I believe that it must be the work of powerful alchemy.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: The Elixir is highly regarded in Liyue, and is said to "re-invoke the radiant dignity within"...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: According to my estimations, my understanding of alchemy will advance by at least a decade if I prove able to synthesize this Elixir!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A decade? That's awesome!

choices.text: As long as the book is accurate, of course.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Don't worry! The author of this book is a genuine genius. They've written all manner of acclaimed essays, to boot.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Alchemy is a most fascinating science. As we seek to uncover the techniques of the ancients, we are also consulting with the research of our contemporaries, constantly evolving and improving.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: That's why I seek out all manner of texts — to uncover what help they may be to my study of alchemy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're a really positive guy, huh, Timaeus?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: If the two of you could lend me a hand, I'm sure that my research will be completed with ease and produce results that Mr. Albedo will acknowledge!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I might even be able to become his assistant and stay with him at his encampment permanently, researching topics of even greater difficulty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you say, {NICKNAME}? Should we help him out?

choices.text: Well, we do need that Crafting Bench...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, guess we're helping him!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Thank you both so much! I'll find an appropriate way to repay you for sure!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Once I'm done synthesizing the Smoldersleet Elixir, you shall be the first to enjoy its miraculous effects. Believe you me, you'll be stronger in a blink of an eye!

choices.text: No need to be so polite...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Never mind medicines or becoming stronger, Paimon just wants some good food!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: That's even easier! Once we finish this task, I'll provide you with the appropriate remuneration and invite you to a restaurant of your choice for a hearty meal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? It's a deal, then!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You assist Timaeus in his attempt to create the legendary Smoldersleet Elixir...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: *sigh* It seems that my current techniques are insufficient to create the Smoldersleet Elixir. Looks like we'll need the help of a specialist...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like Albedo?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: No! Out of the question! Isn't that the same as asking your exam proctor for the answers!?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: If Mr. Albedo found out that I couldn't even make medicine, then it's all the more unlikely that he'll ever acknowledge me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm, you do have a point...

response.speaker: <UNKNOWN_NPC_ID_FORMAT>
response.text: How about asking Sucrose?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Sucrose is far beyond me in her understanding of alchemy, yes, but her field of expertise is essentially unrelated to the Smoldersleet Elixir...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Also, she's usually very busy. I wouldn't want to disturb her...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You could ask Lisa.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Ms. Lisa is currently sorting out the book collection that library has within its walls. It's frighteningly hard work, so I hear... and I doubt she would be any less frightening if we disturbed her.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Whatever the case, we should, ah, probably not bother her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Then doesn't that leave us without any options?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Not exactly. Our help lies not in Mondstadt... but in Liyue.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: The text that I read mentions that "The artificer amidst quiet doors hides, the scented wind in the harbor abides."

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: The "scented wind" is synonymous with the "south wind" in Liyue, so this Elixir Artificer who made our Smoldersleet Elixir must be someone who lives in the southern area of Liyue Harbor.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Consulting this Artificer, then, is our most effective solution.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: So, would you two mind accompanying me to Liyue? I'm... honestly not too familiar with that place.

choices.text: Regarding the meaning of that poem...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Of course! Please have faith in my analytic capabilities!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liyue, huh... That's a long way out.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Oh yes, I've heard that Liyue cuisine is very delicious. Once this is over, we can just eat there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, great idea! Paimon's in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Better watch out, because Paimon's gonna eat every signature dish at Wanmin Restaurant. You can't ever get enough of those, that's for sure!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Don't worry. Compared to the fruits of my research— uh, I mean, a little Mora is nothing compared to the favor I owe the two of you for helping me!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Let's set off immediately!

choices.text: You sure your research funds will hold, Timaeus?
Are you sure of your conclusions?
I don't exactly need external help to become stronger...
Let's help advance his academic career a little...
As long as your estimations are on point, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Let me look at that map... the southern part of Liyue Harbor is known as Chihu Rock, right? That's where we'll find our Elixir Artificer, I'll wager.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, here's Chihu Rock! Let's go have a look around!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello there! Do you know the Elixir Artificer who lives around here?

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: Elixir what now? I've never heard of such a person...

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: Aren't only big shot artisans called something fancy like an "artificer?" I'm afraid someone of my station wouldn't know anyone like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Well, let's go ask someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! We're looking for the Elixir Artificer of Chihu Rock. Would you know where he lives?

dialogues.speaker: Hongyi
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not very familiar with the nicknames that my neighbors have, only their proper recorded names.

dialogues.speaker: Hongyi
dialogues.text: Perhaps you could ask Ying'er from Scent of Spring.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, that makes sense! Ms. Ying'er should totally be familiar with what's going on around here. Let's just go ask her!

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Oh, so glad to see that I'm finally on your mind. And you've brought a friend, too! Here to keep me company, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh boy, Paimon's got a funny feeling about this already...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, Ms. Ying'er, we're here to pay the Elixir Artificer a visit. Do you know where we can find this person?

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Oh my, you've got your foot in another boat already, I see. Ah, I must admit, I'm a little disappointed...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: But I must say that it's a pleasant surprise that you're digging into my deepest secrets like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute! Does this mean that Ms. Ying'er *is* the Elixir Artificer?

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Growing ever smarter, I see. How adorable!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's... unexpected!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: To think that the Elixir Artificer would be so young...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Sure, the feeling is quite different from Mr. Albedo, but there's that same inscrutable aura!

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Ah, looking at your flustered faces, you must have some cares that need lifting. Come now, let's be direct, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels like this situation is about to take an unexpected turn...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Timaeus explain his research into the Smoldersleet Elixir.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Ah, so this alchemist is doing research into this wondrous Smoldersleet Elixir...

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: I'm afraid that I am about to disappoint you.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: The "Smoldersleet Elixir" you seek is just an ancient perfume that is my specialty. It has nothing to do with alchemy.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: A perfume? Isn't that some sort of solid spice?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But it has such a cool name! And the book said that it could make people stronger...

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Hehe, I suspect that must have been a result of the perfume's popularity.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: The ancient writers once emphasized the virtues of "edification through immersion" — that is to say that human temperament and character can be affected by being steeped in aromas and lovely scents.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Those who have used my ancient perfume find themselves becoming magnetic, confident, their relations ever improving, their careers ever climbing, their sailing ever smooth...

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Why, it's almost as if they had truly used an adepti elixir.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: As such, people gave that ancient perfume of mine a suitably poetic name before writing a simple poem to praise its efficacy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: That can't be... Was the essay I read mistaken? Or was my understanding of the poem in error?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Like for example: this elixir is said to "re-invoke the radiant dignity within." Doesn't that mean that it's capable of unlocking a person's inner power and potential, Ms. Ying'er?

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Oh dear. Actually, this phrase refers to a person's demeanor and temperament. What it really means is that the ancient perfume allows people to appear refreshed and radiant.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Not that I blame you, of course. Poetry requires deep study, and it is quite different from the analysis of data and numbers. We are not meant to look at the words in isolation, but as a whole.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: So word-by-word analysis doesn't work in this case?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: But that book mentioned many of the curious effects of the Smoldersleet Elixir. Honestly, I was left speechless as I read them...

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Titillating mysteries are fascinating things, like a lovely silhouette seen through a window screen. So too, do books that record street rumors require a certain artistic license.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Ah, but I must say, that really was high praise...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: How could this be...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So let Paimon get this straight: Timaeus' reference material bragged about the perfume's effects, and then he misread the poem, resulting in his believing that this Smoldersleet Elixir is some super powerful alchemical medicine?

choices.text: Well, can't say I didn't come mentally prepared.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: So in the end, my research was based on incorrect arguments!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Agh... I failed again, and I did a ton of fruitless work to boot!

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Now, now, don't get so down.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: They do say that "the path between mountains leads to new trails, and even the withered wood shall sprout anew"...

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Perhaps the ancient arts of producing perfume might give you a little inspiration and allow you to break through this final bottleneck in producing the medicine you desire?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. Things might have developed weirdly, but you did get pretty far using your own understanding, Timaeus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since Ms. Ying'er's agreed to help, why not give it a go?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who knows, you might make some unexpected gains.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: You're right. Alchemy, too, is a deep science, and this isn't my first failure either. I've got to push through this!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I can usually grasp what I'm reading. This is just a blip!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Even if I can't produce some miracle medicine, improving the alchemical remedies we have currently is an accomplishment nonetheless!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Ms. Ying'er, Traveler, let's head to the nearest Crafting Bench.

choices.text: Feels like par for the course, somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Now, the making of ancient perfumes is quite the delicate process.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Think of your movements as a lover's caress. Gently peel the bud open, remove the petals, and stack them with care.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Thinner petals on top, thicker ones below, leaving appropriate gaps between each, then mash them...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Don't grip your mortar and pestle too tightly. Loose wrists, steady rhythm. Up and down, up and down...

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Wait until the petal sap has oozed out and the base of your mortar and pestle are moist before speeding up.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Uh... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ms. Ying'er, I must say that your choice of words is most, ah, unique! Nonetheless, I understand what you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: The raw materials must be handled carefully and placed into the container in the right order. The timing of immersing them into the base fluid must be precise so that we can better control the temperature...

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Creating alchemical potions of a high quality also requires similarly strict controls.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: Ah, you're quite the bright spark, aren't you? But that's not all.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: The sublimation effect of certain perfumes must be given utmost care. As such, suitable auxiliary materials, such as Mint and Starconch, must be added.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: This way, the perfume's scent will diffuse quickly, allowing everyone around to relax.

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: But this effect cannot be too strong, or the perfume will not endure long.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: ...Sublimate, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I get it! Actually, this aspect of making ancient perfumes is exactly what I'm looking for!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Aerosolized medication can affect both the user and the environment, granting them more obvious effects than ordinary essential oils!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Fine control over the sublimation speeds should allow such agents to last longer than essential oils as well.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, this direction is very promising indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, there's no place in this academic mumbo-jumbo for the likes of us, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's leave them alone for a while, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Under Ying'er's direction, Timaeus tries making an improved alchemical agent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That smells great! Paimon feels refreshed and energized already!

choices.text: It really does perk you up.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: It's a success! I finally succeeded in combining ancient perfume-making with alchemical agents!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Thank you so much, Ms. Ying'er. If not for your expert instruction, there's no way I would have grasped these concepts and made these medicines so easily!

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Oh, come now. Too much humility will make you come off as shallow and overly polite. It was your own knowledge and discernment that proved key to your success.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Well then... Won't you give the fruit of your ardent labor a name?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Let's call them "Smoldersleet Potions," then! They're a combination of your perfume-making techniques and the features of alchemical potions together — a unique blend that will go down in history for sure!

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: Oh my, how you flatter me~

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you know, that name's not all that different from Smoldersleet Elixir...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Well, uh, let's get back on topic!

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Traveler, as promised, you shall be the very first user of the Smoldersleet Potion.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: It could still use some improvement in its current form, so could I trouble you to test its effects for me?

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Its effects should be more obvious in areas where the air flow is gentle.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I've heard that Liyue has some domains in which no one sets foot. I reckon those would be ideal testing grounds!

choices.text: Well, in for one Mora, in for the lot...

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: Then you have my thanks.

response.speaker: Timaeus
response.text: I'll remain here for a while longer to continue my discussions with Ms. Ying'er. Once I get your feedback, I'll make some improvements to the Smoldersleet Potion.

response.speaker: Ying'er
response.text: We'll be waiting for good news from you~

choices.text: Honestly, you've got me pretty excited, too!

talks.objective: Go into the Domain and test the Smoldersleet Potions

dialogues.speaker: Ying'er
dialogues.text: There's still a lot more to learn in the field of perfumes and essential oils. Would you like to hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Of course! In fact, we could keep going for days and nights on end — as long as you don't mind, of course!
